paper_metadata.title: Quantitative EEG Parameters for Prediction of Outcome in Severe Traumatic Brain Injury: Development Study

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the target population (severe TBI in ICU), recruitment period, and setting. Inclusion and exclusion criteria are explicit, and baseline characteristics are reported. While the sample size is small (n=28), the recruitment process appears systematic for the setting.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: All patients with severe TBI, arriving at the ICU of Turku University Hospital during the study period January 2012 to November 2013, were recruited to the study unless they fulfilled the exclusion criteria.
items.reasoning: The source population is clearly defined as severe TBI patients admitted to a specific tertiary ICU.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: All patients with severe TBI... were recruited to the study unless they fulfilled the exclusion criteria.
items.reasoning: The study used a consecutive recruitment strategy at a single center, which is standard for this type of ICU-based prognostic study.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: during the study period January 2012 to November 2013
items.reasoning: The dates are explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: ICU of Turku University Hospital
items.reasoning: The specific hospital and unit are identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: The exclusion criteria for the study were: age less than 18 years at study entry; severely injured scalp... patient gained consciousness before the monitoring could be started... inability to live independently due to preinjury brain disease
items.reasoning: Detailed inclusion (severe TBI by GCS) and exclusion criteria are provided.

items.reasoning: Table 2 provides a comprehensive breakdown of baseline clinical and demographic data.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The attrition rate is low (approx 10%) and the reasons for exclusion (missing follow-up) are clearly stated. Given the severity of the condition, the follow-up rate is acceptable.

items.reasoning: 28/31 (90.3%) of the recruited sample completed the study, which is high for a TBI population.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The QEEG parameters are defined with high technical precision. The measurement is objective, automated, and standardized across all participants, minimizing measurement bias.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: We computed the mean power spectral density (PSD) for each 1-minute period... The power spectrum of the EEG was divided into following frequency bands: delta (1-3.5 Hz), theta (3.5-8 Hz)...
items.reasoning: The technical definitions of the 59 QEEG parameters are very detailed.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.evidence_snippet: The cEEG was recorded using NicoletOne monitoring device... international 10-20 electrode placement system was used with Ag-AgCl subcutaneous wire electrodes
items.reasoning: Standard clinical equipment and validated electrode placement were used.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: For each QEEG parameter we computed the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)
items.reasoning: The study treats the parameters as continuous variables for the primary AUC analysis.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.evidence_snippet: The montage used while computing all the EEG parameters was longitudal bipolar montage consisting of 16 derivations... for all study participants.
items.reasoning: The measurement protocol was standardized, though some patients had fewer electrodes due to injury.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.evidence_snippet: All the QEEG parameters, except the parameters measuring EEG asymmetry were computed for all the subjects in the study
items.reasoning: Complete data was available for the primary parameters in all 28 patients.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.evidence_snippet: Periods that contained less than 3 hours of EEG were ignored.
items.reasoning: The study used a threshold for data inclusion rather than imputation, which is appropriate for this signal-processing context.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The GOS is a standard, validated tool for TBI outcome. The timing of assessment (6-12 months) is appropriate for severe TBI.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.evidence_snippet: The outcomes of the patients were assessed using the Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) evaluated between 6 and 12 months from the injury at a follow-up visit.
items.reasoning: The outcome and its timing are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.evidence_snippet: The outcome was dichotomized to favorable (GOS 4 and 5) and unfavorable (GOS 1-3).
items.reasoning: GOS is the gold standard for TBI prognosis studies.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.evidence_snippet: evaluated between 6 and 12 months from the injury at a follow-up visit.
items.reasoning: The setting (follow-up visit) was consistent for all participants.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for age (a major confounder) and monitors sedation, but the small sample size limits the ability to perform robust multivariable adjustment for other clinical factors (e.g., injury severity, specific treatments).

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.evidence_snippet: Table 2. Patient Characteristics... Age, Sex, GCS, Marshall CT, Medication dosages
items.reasoning: Key clinical confounders were recorded.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.evidence_snippet: Medication dosages (mean ± SD)... Propofol (mg/kg/h), Midazolam (mg/kg/h)...
items.reasoning: Confounders like sedation are precisely defined by dosage.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.evidence_snippet: Medication dosages... obtained from the ICU records.
items.reasoning: Clinical records and standard scales (GCS, Marshall) provide reliable data.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.evidence_snippet: The method and setting... same for all study participants.
items.reasoning: Standard ICU monitoring was used for all.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: No mention of missing confounder data or imputation.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.evidence_snippet: we also computed the AUC for each QEEG after removing the correlation to age using linear regression.
items.reasoning: Age was adjusted for, but other factors (sedation, GCS) were only compared between groups without multivariable adjustment.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: The best QEEG parameters had a statistically significant correlation to the outcome also after removing the correlation to the age
items.reasoning: Adjustment was limited to age; the small sample size (n=28) precluded more complex modeling.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The analysis is appropriate for an 'explorative' or 'development' study. However, the high number of parameters (59) tested against a small sample (n=28) increases the risk of false-positive findings (multiple testing), which the authors acknowledge.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.evidence_snippet: For each QEEG parameter we computed the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)... computed the P value for rejecting the null hypothesis... using the 2-sided Mann-Whitney U test
items.reasoning: The statistical plan is clearly laid out.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.evidence_snippet: This explorative study... studying a wide range of fully automatically extracted QEEG parameters.
items.reasoning: The strategy is exploratory rather than hypothesis-driven, which is acceptable for a development study but carries higher bias risk.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: AUC is equal to the probability that a patient with favorable outcome will have a higher parameter value than patient with unfavorable outcome.
items.reasoning: AUC is an appropriate non-parametric measure for prognostic discrimination.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.evidence_snippet: The entire list of QEEG parameters and the associated statistics can be found in the electronic supplementary material.
items.reasoning: The authors provide the full results for all 59 parameters, reducing the risk of selective reporting.
